{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** Legal (in-house counsel, Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Vendor's Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

The risk-allocation core of this draft is strong for us. Limitation of liability (§ 21), assignment and change of control (§ 24), the licence grant (§ 13.1–13.3), audit rights (§ 22), auto-renewal and renewal uplift (§ 8.2–8.3), warranties (§ 19) and Vendor insurance (§ 18) all meet our preferred positions and require no redline.

The problems are concentrated in the commercial-lock-in and exit provisions, plus two structural gaps. Eight findings sit in walk-away territory: there is **no indemnification clause at all** (Section 20 is simply absent, yet four other sections cross-refer to it), **no transition assistance or data-return/deletion obligation**, and **no Customer termination-for-convenience right** in a three-year term that § 2.1 locks with a USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights." Section 7.2 imposes a disclose-and-match obligation on us (both a de facto exclusivity/ROFR and a Customer-side MFN), § 12.4 imposes a 24-month no-hire and an undefined-scope non-compete on us, § 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction, and § 14.2 vests exclusive Deliverable ownership in Vendor with only a revocable, term-limited licence back to us.

Several of these deviations contradict the Vendor's own acknowledgements in § 12.3 (no exclusivity, no MFN, no minimum-volume, no no-hire commitment by Customer), and § 28.1 contradicts § 28.2 (New York County exclusive jurisdiction). We should press these internal inconsistencies as the cleanest route to the fixes we need.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1 (with 21.2, 21.3, 18.2) | Mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; uncapped Excluded Claims. Preferred position. |
| 2 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment / change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with 24.2–24.4, 13.3) | Consent-free Affiliate/M&A assignment for us; no Vendor repricing or termination on our change of control. |
| 3 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 27.3 | No LD, penalty or exit charge on us; § 27.3 permits termination "without penalty." |
| 4 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 (with 13.2–13.3) | Affiliates and contractors covered; perpetual paid-up licence to delivered Vendor Technology. |
| 5 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 (with 22.2–22.3) | Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, no system access. |
| 6 | Medium | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 14.2 | Vendor owns every Deliverable; we get a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence. Fails the fallback. |
| 7 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation (walk-away)** | § 12.4 | One-way 24-month no-hire covering all Vendor employees, no carve-outs. |
| 8 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8.2 (with 8.3) | 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder with deadline extension; uplift capped at lesser of CPI-U and 3%. |
| 9 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing (walk-away)** | § 10.2 (§ 10 as drafted) | No migration assistance, no data export, no certified deletion; § 16.5 defers to a Section 11 that does not exist. |
| 10 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.2 (with 19.1, 19.3–19.5) | 90-day Deliverable conformity; hosted Services conform for the whole term; disclaimer limited to implied warranties. |
| 11 | Low | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Deviation (walk-away)** | § 7.2 | Disclose-and-match before engaging another provider = de facto exclusivity/ROFR for the full term, no performance exit. |
| 12 | Low | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation (walk-away)** | § 28.1 | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction; conflicts with § 28.2 (New York County). |
| 13 | Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Missing (walk-away)** | Section 20 absent (cross-referred at §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3, 30.5) | No Vendor IP or other indemnity anywhere in the document. |
| 14 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 | CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber/privacy 5M, workers' comp; term plus one year; does not limit liability. |
| 15 | Low | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | **Deviation (walk-away)** | § 7.2 | Open-ended Customer-side duty to disclose and match better third-party terms; contradicts § 12.3. |
| 16 | Low | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | **Deviation (walk-away)** | § 2.1 | USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay for three years "without reduction or termination rights"; contradicts §§ 7.1 and 12.3. |
| 17 | Low | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | **Deviation (walk-away)** | § 12.4 | Term plus 24 months, "any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory," no carve-outs. |
| 18 | Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing (walk-away)** | § 9 (9.1–9.3 only; § 2.1) | For-cause exits only in a three-year term locked by the § 2.1 take-or-pay. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These eight points sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and, absent movement, should be escalated to the business before signature:

1. **No indemnification clause (Section 20 absent).** No Vendor IP indemnity anywhere; §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 all presuppose an indemnity that was never drafted. We propose a new Section 20 at the preferred position (Vendor defence and indemnity for IP, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breaches, gross negligence/wilful misconduct; notice/control/cooperation; procure-modify-replace-refund at 20.5, which also cures the § 9.3 cross-reference; narrow Customer indemnity for Customer content and Customer's breach of law). No super-cap is needed because § 21.3 already treats indemnification as an Excluded Claim.
2. **No transition assistance or data return (§ 10).** Insert a Section 10.3: up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter, with a routine-backup/legal-retention carve-out consistent with § 16.5.
3. **No Customer termination for convenience (§ 9).** Insert a Section 9.4 giving us 30 days' notice convenience termination with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and carve it out of § 2.1 so the right is effective.
4. **§ 2.1 take-or-pay.** USD 2,000,000 per year for three years with no reduction or termination rights; move to pay-only-for-Services-ordered-or-used, or at minimum to the fallback (current 12-month term only, reducible on 30 days' notice, trued up not penalised).
5. **§ 7.2 disclose-and-match — exclusivity/ROFR.** Delete the Customer-side obligation; it applies to all Services for the full term with no category limit, sunset or performance exit.
6. **§ 7.2 disclose-and-match — Customer-side MFN.** Delete; unlimited as to product, duration and comparability, with no reasonable-comparison carve-outs. Any Vendor-granted MFN in our favour is retained.
7. **§ 12.4 non-compete and no-hire.** Delete the non-compete (term plus 24 months, undefined scope, no internal-development or acquisition carve-out); narrow the no-hire to a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel involved in the Services with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.
8. **§ 28.1 Singapore law and exclusive Singapore venue.** Move to New York law and New York County courts, harmonising with § 28.2.

Items 4–7 each contradict § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that we have made no minimum-volume, exclusivity, most-favoured-customer or no-hire commitment. We should lead with that inconsistency.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the four remediable deviations and three insertions: § 14.2 (Deliverable ownership flipped to Customer with express assignment, preserving Vendor's retained Vendor Technology rights under § 14.3, or at minimum the fallback perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable licence to use and modify), § 7.2 (delete both the exclusivity and MFN limbs), § 12.4 (delete the non-compete), § 28.1 (New York law and forum, confining § 28.2's carve-out to the New York County courts), plus new Sections 20, 10.3 and 9.4.
2. **Re-draft three proposals before they go out.** Our proposed language for the § 12.4 no-hire narrowing, the § 2.1 take-or-pay reset and the § 9.4 convenience-termination insertion did not clear verification; these need manual drafting and re-checking rather than release as-is.
3. **Confirm the deal team's position on § 2.1** before we negotiate: whether we can accept any committed volume, and if so on what fallback parameters.
4. **Raise the drafting defects with Vendor's counsel** as a package: Section 20 missing entirely, § 16.5 referring to a non-existent Section 11, § 9.3 referring to Section 20.5, § 28.1 conflicting with § 28.2, § 14.2 conflicting with §§ 13.2–13.3 and 14.3, and § 12.3 conflicting with §§ 2.1, 7.2 and 12.4.
5. **Request the missing service-level exhibit** referenced in § 2.2. It is not in the document, so we cannot confirm that service credits run in our favour or assess the § 9.3 "repeatedly misses a critical service level" trigger.
6. **No action required** on §§ 8, 13.1, 18, 19, 21, 22, 24 and 27.3 — these meet our preferred positions and we should protect them in any exchange of drafts."}
